Base directory for this skill: D:\Repos\angular-jig\.claude\skills\slice-generator

# Slice generator

Three kinds of code in this app are generated, not hand-written: the domain entity (model, zod schema, service, example data), the schema-driven form component, and the manage screen (a routed CRUD list). You describe the entity once in a spec file and the `slice` schematic emits all of it in the house shape: sealed spartan primitives, signal forms with `validateStandardSchema`, a component-scoped ViewModel, icons registered with `provideIcons`, unit tests for the service and the ViewModel.

If you are about to write a `*.model.ts`, a `*.schema.ts`, a `*.service.ts`, a `*-form` component under `src/app/ui/`, or a list screen with a table, a create/edit dialog and a delete confirmation, stop and write a spec instead.

## The workflow

1. Write or extend `specs/<entity>.json` (kebab-case file name, for example `specs/book.json`). It must be valid against `schematics/slice/spec.schema.json`. The schema checks structure; the schematic also checks the cross-field rules (field references, example rows, kinds) and prints every problem it finds.
2. Run `ng generate slice --spec specs/<entity>.json`.
3. Wire the result in by hand: add a navigation link to a manage screen, show entity data on a dashboard, build any bespoke screen on top of the generated service.
4. If a generated file needs a small addition, make it in place with Edit. If it has the wrong shape, change the spec and regenerate that kind with `ng generate slice --spec specs/<entity>.json --kinds <kind> --force`. Do not rewrite a generated file, move it, rename it or write a copy beside it: the next regeneration would erase the rewrite, and a copy drifts from the one the spec describes.

When a file the run would write already exists, the schematic looks at it first. If it is identical to what the generator emits (line endings aside), it is skipped and the run prints `Unchanged: <path>`, so rerunning over your own unchanged output is safe and changes nothing. If it carries the placeholder marker `slice:placeholder`, it is replaced without `--force`: a placeholder holds nothing you need (the starting app may hold one, such as `src/app/heroes/heroes.*`). Any other existing file stops the run: it fails with an `already exists` line for each such file and writes nothing, which protects hand-written code and your in-place edits. `--force` (the standard `ng generate` flag) replaces every such file the requested kinds produce. Use it only when every file it would replace is this generator's output or something you mean to lose, and pair it with `--kinds` so it touches only the kind whose shape you changed. Check with `git status --short <path>` for each file the run would replace: nothing is committed between stages, so every file a stage created is untracked and shows up there. If hand-written work you need is in the way, do not force: keep it and build on the generated service instead.

The schematic reads its own source from `schematics/`. That folder is read-only for you: you can read it to understand an output, but a change to what the generator emits is not yours to make. Work through the spec.

## Generating one kind at a time

`--kinds` takes a comma-separated subset of the spec's `kinds`, for example `ng generate slice --spec specs/loan.json --kinds entity` now and `--kinds form,manage` later. Without it, the run generates every kind the spec lists. A kind whose dependencies are not generated in the same run must find them on disk: `form` needs the entity's model, schema and service, and `manage` needs those plus the form component. If they are missing, the run stops, names the missing files and the command that makes them, and writes nothing. A kind the spec does not list is refused.

## Generated files

Every TypeScript file the schematic writes starts with this line:

    // @generated by the slice schematic from its spec. Edit in place; reshape via the spec and --force.

The generator writes, under `src/app/`, every `*.model.ts`, `*.schema.ts`, `*.service.ts`, `*.service.spec.ts` and `*-example-data.ts` of an entity, and everything under `ui/<entity>-form/`. In this app a hook enforces the part that marks a hand-built domain, but only for an entity that has a spec at `specs/<entity>.json` (for example `specs/book.json`): for that entity, a Write that creates its `*.model.ts`, `*.schema.ts` or `*-example-data.ts`, or any file under `ui/<entity>-form/`, is denied with the command that generates it. A Write over a file that carries `slice:placeholder` is denied whatever the entity. Hand-written schemas and models for features without an entity spec, such as a wizard's `<feature>.schema.ts`, are not policed. Services are not policed by the hook, because the app has services the generator does not make, such as a theme service; an entity's service still comes from the generator with the rest of the entity. Edit is allowed, so you fill and adjust generated files in place. After a shell command, the same hook reports any of those policed files that does not start with the header, because the generator did not write it.

## Order matters when entities reference each other

A `ref` field imports the target entity's service. Generate the entity that is referenced first. If `loan` references `book` and `member`, generate `book` and `member` before `loan`, or `loan` will not compile.

## What each kind emits

`entity` writes, under `src/app/<entity>/`:

- `<entity>.model.ts`: the interface and one string-union type per enum field.
- `<entity>.schema.ts`: the zod schema (one entry per field with `inForm` true, with `.meta({...} satisfies FormFieldMeta)`), exporting `<entity>Schema` and `type <Entity>FormModel = z.infer<...>`.
- `<entity>.service.ts`: a root-provided `<Entity>Service` with a private signal seeded from example data, a readonly list signal named after `plural`, `byId`, `create`, `update`, `remove`. If the entity has `ref` fields, the service also prunes references to records that no longer exist, and a many-ref field gets a `for<Target>(id)` lookup.
- `<entity>-example-data.ts`: the spec's `examples`, marked as example data. Ids are assigned `"1"`, `"2"`, and so on, by row position.
- `<entity>.service.spec.ts`: tests for seeding, create, update, remove, and reference pruning.

`form` writes `src/app/ui/<entity>-form/<entity>-form.ts`, `<entity>-form.html` and `<entity>-form.css`: a standalone `<Entity>Form` component built from the schema. It has one `hlm-field` block per form field, chosen by type, an `initialValue` input reseeded through a `linkedSignal` compared by value, a `save<Entity>` output and a `cancel` output. A `ref` field also gets a `<field>Options` input that the parent fills.

`manage` writes, under `src/app/<plural>/`, a routed screen:

- `<plural>.ts`: a thin component with `providers: [<Plural>ViewModel]`, `templateUrl` and `styleUrl`.
- `<plural>.view-model.ts`: the ViewModel with search, the select and toggle filters, the optional sort, editing state, `startCreate`, `startEdit`, `cancel`, `save`, `remove`, and the option lists for ref fields.
- `<plural>.html`: a table in a scroll container (no stacked cards), the select and toggle filters the spec asks for, an edit dialog hosting the generated form, a create dialog hosting it too (or, with `createRoute`, a create link instead), a delete confirmation dialog, an empty state, and, when the spec sets `summary`, a footer with a count, plus a "sorted by" line only when `sort` is also set. Classes are BEM on the `<plural>` block.
- `<plural>.css`: a layout-only stylesheet for those BEM classes.
- `<plural>.view-model.spec.ts`: ViewModel tests.
- It also adds a lazy route for `plural` to `src/app/app.routes.ts`, unless a route already loads `./<plural>/<plural>` under any path: then it keeps that route and its path, and adds none. If it cannot find the `routes` array literal it stops with an error instead of guessing.

## What is not generated

- Navigation. The route exists after generation; add the link to the shell yourself.
- Dashboards, stat tiles, detail pages, tabs, wizards, settings screens, and any other bespoke screen. Build those by hand on top of the generated services, with their own ViewModels.
- Cross-entity computed columns (for example a count of related records). Add a method to a hand-written ViewModel, or a bespoke screen.
- Backend access. Services are in-memory and seeded from the example data.
- More than three filters, clickable column sorting, avatar or custom cells, columns that show a `ref` field, and multi-select form controls.

## The spec

A spec is pure data. Unknown keys are rejected everywhere. Free text (labels, placeholders, help, enum options, example strings) may not contain `<`, `>`, `{`, `}`, a backtick, `$` or a backslash, and has a length cap. Identifiers are pinned by pattern: `entity` is PascalCase (`Loan`, `ReadingList`), `plural` is lowercase kebab-case (`loans`), field names are camelCase and cannot be `id` (ids are generated), icons look like `lucideTarget`.

Top level:

- `entity`, `plural`: identifiers.
- `labels`: `{ "singular": "loan", "plural": "loans" }`, the words used in screen text.
- `kinds`: any of `entity`, `form`, `manage`. `form` needs `entity`; `manage` needs both.
- `fields`: the field list, in display order.
- `examples`: optional rows of example data, one value for every field, validated against the field definitions.
- `manage`: required when `kinds` includes `manage`, forbidden otherwise.

Every field has `name`, `type`, `label`, `required`, and optionally `inForm` (default true), `placeholder`, `help`. A field with `inForm: false` is model-only: it is not in the schema or the form, and it needs a `default`, which `create` uses. Field types:

| type | extra keys | becomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `default` | text input |
| `text` | `default` | textarea |
| `number` | `min`, `max`, `default` | number input |
| `boolean` | `default` | switch |
| `enum` | `options` (list of strings), `default` | select |
| `date` | `default` | text input holding an ISO date string, `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `ref` | `ref: { entity, plural, label }`, `many`, `default` | select whose options come from the target entity's service |

Rules that trip people up:

- `required` must be `true` for `number`, `boolean` and `enum`: they always have a value.
- A required single `ref` must be in the form (`inForm` true); only an optional single ref can be model-only, with `"default": null`.
- At least one field must be in the form, even for an entity-only spec.
- A `ref` points at one id (`string`, or `null` when not required). `many: true` makes it a list of ids; a many ref cannot be in the form, so it also needs `inForm: false` and `"default": []`.
- Dates are ISO strings, never `Date` objects.
- `ref.label` names the field of the target entity shown in the select. It must be a string-valued field of that entity: `string`, `text`, `enum` or `date`, never a number, boolean or ref. When the target's spec is at `specs/<entity>.json` the generator checks this (and the target's `plural`) and stops with a readable error; if that spec is not there, nothing checks it and a wrong label surfaces as a build error.

The `manage` section:

```json
"manage": {
  "icon": "lucideBookMarked",
  "createLabel": "New loan",
  "createRoute": "/loans/new",
  "columns": [
    { "field": "reference" },
    { "field": "status", "badge": { "variants": { "Returned": "default", "Overdue": "destructive" }, "fallback": "secondary" } },
    { "field": "borrowedOn" }
  ],
  "search": ["reference", "branch"],
  "filters": [
    { "field": "status", "control": "select" },
    { "field": "extended", "control": "toggle", "label": "Extended only", "icon": "lucideRefreshCw" }
  ],
  "sort": { "field": "borrowedOn", "direction": "desc" },
  "summary": true
}
```

- `columns`: the table columns in order. The first must be a `string` or `text` field and doubles as the row title. Any `enum` column can carry a `badge` mapping option values to spartan badge variants (`default`, `secondary`, `destructive`, `outline`) with a `fallback`.
- `search`: `string` or `text` fields matched by the search box.
- `filters`: optional, one to three entries, each on a different field. `{ "field", "control": "select" }` is a dropdown on any `enum` field, listing its options plus All. `{ "field", "control": "toggle", "label", "icon" }` is a toggle button: on a `boolean` field it filters to true; on an `enum` field add `"value": "Critical"` and it filters to that option. A toggle field must be a form field, and so must the search fields.
- `sort`: optional, `{ "field", "direction": "asc" | "desc" }`, the fixed order of the rows. The field is a `string`, `text`, `number`, `date` or `enum` field. There is no clickable column sorting.
- `summary`: optional boolean. `true` adds a footer with the filtered count out of the total, plus the sort order when `sort` is set.
- `createRoute`: optional, an app path such as `/loans/new`. The create button becomes a link to that route instead of opening the create dialog, for a list whose records are created on a screen of their own. Editing and deleting stay in dialogs.
- `icon` and each toggle `icon` must be real Lucide export names from `@ng-icons/lucide`. The generator does not check that the name exists in the installed package, so confirm it if the build reports a missing export.

`schematics/slice/fixtures/` holds complete, valid specs to copy from.

# Capstone build spec: the kitchen-sink Tour of Heroes

This is the conformance target for the capstone build. It is intent plus decisions, not pixels: a low-fidelity layout, build guidelines, a theme palette, and an icon scheme. Build to this with the real sealed spartan primitives and the MVVM pattern, under all gates. Do NOT chase a pixel-perfect mock.

`prototype/tour-of-heroes.html` is a colour-and-mood reference ONLY. It is known to be non-responsive (measured: 19 responsive-gate violations) and its CSS and layout mechanics must not be copied. Take the look and feel from it; take the structure, palette, icons, and responsive rules from this document.

## How to use this

- The app is "Hero Ops Console": Tour of Heroes reimagined as a superhero agency's mission control. That framing is what makes the kitchen sink coherent (a roster, missions, threats, recruiting) rather than a component zoo.
- Build every screen responsive-correct at 375px, 768px, and 1280px. The Part 5 responsive gate is on: no horizontal page scroll, no element escaping the viewport, no clipped content at any of the three widths. This is the bar the mock failed and the build must clear.

```
page background          #f6f7fa      #0e1018
foreground (text)        #1b1e2b      #eceef6
card / popover           #ffffff      #171a26
muted surface            #eef0f6      #1e2231
muted foreground         #5b6072      #9aa0b4
border / input           #e4e7ef      #272b3b

sidebar foreground       #eceef6      #eceef6
sidebar muted            #9aa0b4      #8b90a6
sidebar active bg        #2a2f45      #20263c
```

```
-----                 -----------

nav: Roster           lucideUsers
nav: Missions         lucideTarget   (or lucideRadar)
nav: Threats          lucideShieldAlert
nav: Recruit          lucideUserPlus

search                lucideSearch
notifications         lucideBell
edit                  lucidePencil
retire / delete       lucideTrash2
deploy                lucideCrosshair
back                  lucideChevronLeft
select chevron        lucideChevronDown
stat: heroes          lucideUserCheck
stat: missions live   lucideActivity
stat: avg power       lucideZap
stat: threats         lucideShieldAlert

```

Structure and regions, not styling. Each note says what happens at 375px.

App shell (all screens):

```
+--------+-------------------------------------------------+
| RAIL   |  TOPBAR: [menu] crumbs .... [search][bell][thm][av] |
| (dark) +-------------------------------------------------+
| brand  |                                                 |
| ------ |   ROUTED SCREEN CONTENT (scrolls)               |
| nav x6 |                                                 |
| ------ |                                                 |
| user   |                                                 |
+--------+-------------------------------------------------+

       CLOSED drawer must be display:none or aria-hidden, NOT just
       translated off-screen, or the responsive gate flags it as an
       element escaping the viewport. Topbar search collapses to an
       icon that expands, or drops below the crumbs.
```

Dashboard:

```
[ Operations Dashboard ]                        [ + Recruit ]
[ stat ][ stat ][ stat ][ stat ]      <- grid, auto-fit min ~210px
[ Top heroes this cycle ]             [ View all roster ]
[ hero ][ hero ][ hero ][ hero ]      <- grid, auto-fill min ~230px
[ Roster ]                            [ 42 heroes ]
[ ============ ROSTER TABLE ============ ]
375px: stat tiles -> 1 per row; hero cards -> 1-2 per row; table below.
```

Roster table:

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| [search........]  [class v]                    [ + Recruit ] |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| HERO            | CLASS  | POWER | STATUS   | CLEAR | ACTIONS |
| (av) Name/ID    | badge  |  88   | pill     | Tier4 | edit del|
| ...                                                          |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| 42 of 42 heroes                          sorted by power     |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+

       make the gate pass: (a) wrap the table in an overflow-x:auto
       container so the CONTAINER scrolls and the page does not (the
       gate exempts intentional scroll containers); or (b) switch to a
       stacked card list below ~640px (each hero a card). (b) is the
       nicer result; (a) is the cheaper one. Do NOT let the page itself
       scroll sideways.
```

Hero detail:

```
[< Back to roster]
[ (AV lg) ID / Name / Alias / badges ]            [Deploy][Retire]
[ Overview | Powers | Missions | Edit ]           <- tabs
Overview:  [ Field summary + 3 mini-stats ]  [ Dossier k/v ]
Powers:    [ power meters ]                   [ ability badges ]
Missions:  [ list of deployments + result badges ]
Edit:      [ schema form: name, alias, class(select), power(number),
             notes(textarea), active(switch) ; Cancel / Save ]

       tab strip scrolls horizontally if needed; detail header wraps.
```

## Build guidelines

Component map (region -> spartan primitive):

- Navigation rail: `hlm-sidebar` and its parts (`HlmSidebarMenu*`, `HlmSidebarGroup*`, trigger, rail). Let it own its mobile off-canvas behaviour.
- Top bar controls: `hlmBtn` (icon buttons), `hlmInput` (search), `hlm-tooltip` on icon-only buttons, `hlm-avatar` for the account chip.
- Stat tiles and hero cards: `hlm-card` and its parts; `hlm-badge` for trends and classes; `hlm-avatar` for hero portraits.
- Roster: `hlm-table` (with its header/row/cell parts), `hlm-select` for the class filter, `hlmInput` for search, `hlm-badge` for class and status, `hlmBtn` for actions.
- Detail: `hlm-tabs`, `hlm-avatar`, `hlm-badge`; the edit form uses `hlm-field` + `hlm-label` + `hlmInput` + `hlm-select` + `hlm-switch` + a textarea; retire uses `hlm-dialog`. Toast/feedback via whatever spartan provides (sonner/toast) or a small local one.

- Each routed feature screen (Dashboard, Roster, HeroDetail, Recruit) gets a ViewModel: an `@Injectable` service holding all logic and state as signals, unit-testable with no DOM.

- Forms are schema-driven with zod (the existing house pattern): a zod schema is the single source of truth, the model is `z.infer<typeof schema>`, validation flows through `validateStandardSchema`, no per-field validators, no reactive or template-driven forms.

- No horizontal page scroll at any breakpoint. Reach for the layout grammar: `grid` for regions with responsive column counts (`grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4`), `flex` with `flex-wrap` for button rows, never fixed pixel widths that cannot shrink.
- Any wide block (the table) either scrolls inside its own `overflow-x:auto` container or restructures (cards) below a breakpoint. The page body never scrolls sideways.
- The off-canvas drawer must be `display:none` or `aria-hidden` when closed, not parked off-screen, so the gate does not read it as an escaping element.
- Watch the small ones: the mock leaked 4px at desktop widths. A stray `100vw`, a negative margin, or a `min-w` that will not shrink is usually the cause. The gate catches these; do not ship them.

Layout grammar (enforced by the Part 2 gate): grid for two-dimensional regions, flex for single-axis runs, no nested flex faking a grid, tokens instead of literal colours or pixel values in any hand-written CSS.

Running the responsive auditor on this rich layout surfaced that off-canvas navigation (the standard mobile drawer) reads as `element-escape` because a translated-off-screen element has a negative x. The simple Part 5 slices had no sidebar, so this never appeared. Before the capstone run, the Part 5 spec and auditor/gate need an exemption: an element that is `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, or `aria-hidden="true"` (a deliberately-hidden drawer) is not an escape. Decide the rule, write it into `harness/responsive-spec.md`, and update the auditor and the gate together (they stay two independent encodings of one spec). This is part of the capstone's constitution work, not a bug to hide.

## Content (example data, hero-agency specific)

Reuse the roster from the mock (Silverwing, Dr. Ion, Vantablack, Aurora Vale, Magnetar, The Tinkerer, Halcyon, Rift, Ember Cho, Null, Grond, Ms. Meridian) with their power classes (Aerial, Energy, Psionic, Tech, Mutant, Cosmic, Enhanced), power index (0-100), status (Active/Injured/Reserve/MIA), clearance tier, mission counts, and success rates. Mark it plainly as example data. The specifics (threat tiers, power classes, clearance) are the detail that makes this a real console rather than a generic CRUD table.

The hero domain is generated under `src/app/hero/`, and `ng build` compiles. The generated service spec passes 4 of 4.

I ran exactly `npx ng g slice --spec specs/hero.json --kinds entity`. It wrote five files, each starting with the `@generated` header:

- `hero.model.ts`: the `Hero` interface and the `HeroPowerClass`, `HeroStatus` and `HeroClearance` union types.
- `hero.schema.ts`: `heroSchema` with field labels on `.meta()`, and `HeroFormModel`. `clearance` is left out of the form because the spec sets `inForm: false` on it.
- `hero.service.ts`: `HeroService`, root-provided, with the roster as signal state, plus `heroes`, `byId`, `create`, `update` and `remove`.
- `hero-example-data.ts`: the 12 example heroes from the spec, marked as example data.
- `hero.service.spec.ts`: the service tests.

I did not touch `specs/hero.json` or any hand-written file, and I built no screen. The old `src/app/heroes/` placeholder is still there, unchanged.

Two things to know:

- The generated `HeroService` uses `@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })`, as the generator emits it. CLAUDE.md prefers `@Service` for new singletons. I left it because the generator owns that file and the spec asked for root provision, not a style change. Say if you want it switched.
- The build prints a bundle-budget warning (561.64 kB against a 500 kB budget). It is a warning, not an error, and I did not investigate its cause.
